messages:
Mira: quick question — we hit a confusing case in prod. We have a rollout policy that routes 10% traffic to model-v2 for a canary, but the feature-flag `model_v2_enabled` in Flags service is OFF for everyone. Which should win at request time?
Toni: ah yeah this comes up a lot. Are you seeing requests actually go to v2 or not?
Mira: not, traffic looks 0% to v2 in our traces. Console rollout page shows the split as 10%, but the effective traffic is 0%.
Raj: so there are two separate systems: the rollout engine (console -> runtime polices) and the feature-flag service. Historically we treated flags as a user-facing guard that can short-circuit model selection. Rollouts are a routing layer. We never fully documented precedence.
Selena: tl;dr we need an explicit resolution order. Right now runtime applies routing, then the app consults flags, but some SDKs check flags first. :facepalm:
Cam: repro steps? can you paste the rollout JSON and the flag value?
Mira: pasted — rollout policy: ```{ "route": [{"variant":"model-v2","pct":10},{"variant":"model-v1","pct":90}], "guards": ["region==us-west"] }``` Flag: `model_v2_enabled=false` (global).
Vince: that JSON is fine. If the SDK calls feature-flag check before asking runtime for a route, flag=false wins. If runtime makes route decision and then the serving layer checks flag to allow the chosen variant, route wins.
Toni: so we have a race of semantics: "routing vs authorization". Which semantics do we want? Options: 1) routing first, flags only for final allow/deny 2) flags first (feature toggles can opt-out entire behavior) 3) unified policy engine where flags are just another guard in rollout rules.
Raj: I prefer #3 — put flags as guards inside rollout policies. That gives a single decision path and avoids SDK divergence. But we need migration tooling.
Selena: agreed, but we also need backward compatibility. Many apps rely on flags as global feature toggle (e.g., kill-switch). If we make them guards only, how do we keep kill-switch semantics?
Cam: simple: support a special boolean in flags: `global_override=true|false` that forces off before routing. Or have explicit precedence metadata on flags: `precedence: global|guard`
Mira: both approaches seem fine. Also we should show on console the "effective decision" with reason — e.g., "route decided model-v2 (10%) but blocked by flag:model_v2_enabled=false". That would help debugging.
Vince: +1 to effective decision and telemetry. We should record resolution path in traces: [routing_decision, flag_check, final_variant]. Also create an alert when console route != observed traffic by >5% for 10m.
Toni: API change required. Either: a) define a deterministic server-side evaluation order (recommended), or b) expose both checks to client and leave to SDKs (bad idea).
Raj: propose: server-side unified evaluation order: 1) global overrides (flags with precedence=global) 2) rollout guards (including flag-based guards) 3) routing split 4) post-route allow/deny (safety checks). Documented and enforced in runtime.
Selena: can we add a `resolution_trace` field to the `/evaluate-rollout` API returning something like: "trace": ["global_flag_off","guard_region_mismatch","route: model-v1"]? That will help console and SDKs.
Cam: +1. Also flag-service-bot should emit a warning when a flag change affects active rollouts. eg: "flag model_v2_enabled set to false, affected rollouts: 12"
flag-service-bot: automated notice: "flag model_v2_enabled changed (false). Detected 4 rollouts referencing this flag."
deploy-bot: deploy job #842 completed: rollout-engine@canary -> v0.24.3 (runtime precedence fixes)
Mira: great — next steps? I can spin up a tiny RFC: runtime evaluation order + console effective-decision UI + API `resolution_trace`.
Toni: please include migration path for existing flag-as-kill-switch uses and a short checklist for SDK owners.
Vince: add telemetry event `rollout_resolution` with fields: route_pct, flags_checked, overridden_by_flag (bool), final_variant.
Raj: I'll add validation in console that warns when a flag is referenced by a rollout (cross-ref) and can block rollout publish if you opt-in.
Selena: sounds good. Mira — can you file an RFC and tag me + Raj + Vince? Also create a quick playbook for oncall if a rollout/flag mismatch causes incidents.
Mira: on it. filing RFC now. thanks all :+1:
